learning_objective: The learner will identify the seven parts of an interactive quiz question from a description of how each looks, with at least 6 of 7 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: infographic **sim-id:** quiz-question-anatomy
**Library:** html
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Remember
**Bloom Verb:** identify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will identify the seven parts of an interactive quiz question from a description of how each looks, with at least 6 of 7 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Multiple-Choice Question, Distractor Quality, Feedback Message, Question Difficulty, Question Bank (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** In quiz mode the learner clicks the marker that matches a visual hint. A click is correct when it matches the marker named in the Hint column of Content. Mastery is at least 6 of 7 correct on the first attempt. Hovering in explore mode is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) The distractors are decoration. (2) Feedback appears only for wrong answers. (3) The difficulty tag is a score. **Instructional Rationale:** Identifying the parts of a question is a Remember-level task, and an illustration of one quiz card gives each part a place. The quiz asks the learner to recognize a part by its look, which is how they will spot it in a real quiz. **Content:** The illustration is a text-free flat drawing of one quiz card. At the top is a block of three thin lines. Below it are four rows, each with a round selector, and one row carries a check icon. Under the rows is a panel with a speech-bubble icon holding two thin lines. In the upper right corner are two small tags, one with a target icon and one with a gauge icon. At the lower left is a small button with a circular arrow icon. The seven markers: | # | Label | Hint (describes the look, not the name) | Description | Tip | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Stem | The block of three thin lines at the top of the card. | The question or incomplete statement that the learner answers. | Make the stem clear enough that a learner who knows the answer can give it without reading the options. | | 2 | Key | The option row with a check icon. | The one correct answer. | Make sure only one option can be defended as correct. | | 3 | Distractors | The three option rows without a check icon. | The wrong options, written to reflect likely misconceptions. | Give each distractor a reason a learner might choose it. | | 4 | Feedback message | The panel with a speech-bubble icon under the options. | The text shown after an answer, which explains why. | Write feedback for every option, not only for the key. | | 5 | Outcome tag | The small tag with a target icon at the upper right. | Links the question to the learning outcome it checks. | Use the tag to confirm that every outcome has questions. | | 6 | Difficulty tag | The small tag with a gauge icon at the upper right. | Marks how hard the question is expected to be. | Mix easy, medium, and hard questions across a quiz. | | 7 | Retry control | The small button with a circular arrow at the lower left. | Lets the learner try again, or draw a fresh question from the bank. | Allow retries, because practice needs repetition. | **Provenance:** The parts follow the chapter sections on multiple-choice questions, feedback, distractor quality, question difficulty, and the question bank. The illustration is synthetic, and the sim labels the card "illustrative example". **Rules:** Each hint matches exactly one marker. The illustration contains no text, so every label comes from the table above. Markers are numbered 1 to 7 in the order of the table. Marker 3 covers all three distractor rows as one marker. **Learner Activity:** 1. In explore mode the learner hovers or clicks a marker and reads its label, description, and tip. 2. In quiz mode the sim shows a hint. 3. The learner clicks the marker they think the hint describes. 4. If the first click is wrong, the sim says so and lets the learner try once more. If the second click is also wrong, the sim reveals the marker and its description. 5. After all 7 hints the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 7 hints in a shuffled order, two attempts each. Only a correct first click counts as evidence. Correct: "Correct: [label]. [Description]". First wrong click: "Not quite. Look again at the hint: [hint]". Second wrong click: "This is [label]. [Description]". The summary shows "[n] of 7 correct on the first attempt". At 6 or more it adds "You can read a quiz question." Below 6 it lists the labels of the missed parts. **Starting State:** The illustration with seven numbered markers, explore mode active, and the prompt "Hover a marker to see what it is." **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says a multiple-choice question has a stem, a key, and distractors, that a feedback message explains why, and that questions can be tagged by outcome and difficulty in a question bank.
